So, last night I started up a slack team to talk about moving voat onto a more open stack, and effectively doing the legwork so that putt could make the transition to lower cost providers with a minimum of effort. Initially, I thought this would require a considerable rewrite of the Voat codebase, but after discussion, it appears that, at least initially, docker is going to be the answer we advocate for.

What that means is that we need some of you guys who are experienced in docker (and hopefully people who have hardware to lab on, though it's by no means a requirement) to help us out to save this site. Ideally, we want to have a fully functional, fully tested version of the site running on a test server before we test on a different cloud provider, then, after we have figured that out, approach puttitout, and have him port the site over.

Anyone interested in helping, please join us in slack
Goats with docker experience needed: Help us make voat cheaper and scaleable!

Here is a rundown of the requirements:

Tech Stack: https://docs.docker.com/compose/aspnet-mssql-compose/ https://hub.docker.com/r/microsoft/dotnet-framework

App: https://github.com/voat/voat/tree/Dev

Possible Dependencies: Markdowndeep (http://www.toptensoftware.com/markdowndeep))
Entity Framework (https://entityframework.codeplex.com))
WebApiThrottle (https://github.com/stefanprodan/WebApiThrottle))
SignalR (https://github.com/SignalR/SignalR))
OpenGraph-Net (https://github.com/ghorsey/OpenGraph-Net))
.NET Image Library (https://www.nuget.org/packages/ImageLibrary))
HtmlAgilityPack (http://www.nuget.org/packages/HtmlAgilityPack))
Bootstrap (http://getbootstrap.com))
jQuery (http://jquery.com))

We will eventually need to provision a 4-8GB of RAM server to setup a staging server on a provider like Linode, or OVH, or other lower cost provider.

Intentions: Show Voat's founder we can cut hosting costs using Linux containers, implement better caching, load-balancing, etc. then potentially rewrite Voat using a micro-service architecture with a distributed multi-instance devops model.

Currently Voat is dependent on .Net Framework which is Windows only. This weekend I will be looking into and probably posting findings on what is needed to migrate to .Net core.

I suspect that some of the nuget packages are going to be tricky to migrate or replace specifically OpenGraph-Net, Markdowndeep, SignalR, and .NetImageLibrary, HtmlAgilityPack

EntityFramework and WebApiThrottle both have direct .net core ports already

While there are alternatives to each changing the code over will be work and take time to ensure there isn't any bugs introduced

An option is to migrate and refactor voat into smaller projects and converting them into .net core/standard projects along the way.

.Net Framework in a Docker container: https://hub.docker.com/r/microsoft/dotnet-framework

Looks like it runs in a container just fine (granted I don't know shit about .Net). Microsoft has a full partnership with Docker and has worked pretty hard to get their various libraries and frameworks working in containers.

From there, its just a matter of installing the various dependencies and configuring them properly.

That's the hope at least. I'm sure there might be some challenges but if we can get a repo going we can all work through them together.
That is a windows container. While it will still work I suspect that porting to .Net core will be cheaper in the long run.
I think they're looking at porting to a more agnostic programming language, but not opposed to someone porting to .Net core if it helps in the short term.
